description_en: The Mahābuddha Mandira is one of the most famous Buddhistśikharastyled temples in Patan. Although the temple is often called Mahābuddha Mandira, it is in fact avihāra.It is also known as Bodhimaṇḍapa Vihāra, and is a branch of Oku Bāhāḥ (Rudravarṇa Mahāvihāra,LAL2260). This east-facing temple is located to the south of Sundhārā, on the way to Uku Bāhāḥ. Its main entrance is decorated withaṣṭamaṅgalasand various other motifs. After crossing the entrance and passing through a narrow alley, one arrives at another door, through which one can find images of Mahākāla, Gaṇeśa and Hāratī.The temple complex can be accessed via a narrow alleyway that is 2 meters wide and 22 meters long. The entrance is clearly marked by a decorative gateway between two residential buildings. The mainśikharatemple is built on a frontal courtyard measuring 10 m × 10 m. Theśikharafaces east and has adharmadhātu maṇḍalaand a colonnaded structure in front of it. A smallśikharatemple of Māyādevī can be found on the southern side of this courtyard, southwest of the Mahābuddha temple, and sits upon a square base of 2.4 m × 2.4 m. A raised platform 57 cm high and measuring 385 cm × 385 cm is located 2 m to the west of the main temple structure. The courtyard is now surrounded by tall residential buildings; these were constructed at a later date.The tall, slimśikharatemple has six storeys and is home to the Akṣobhya Buddha. The temple structure is constructed in terracotta bricks with thousands of images of Buddha attached to them. This structure is unique to Nepal. The eastern side of the temple has two intermediate colonnaded vestibules with stone pillars that lead to the central sanctum. A circumambulatory passage (55 cm wide) can be followed around the main sanctum. The external wall contains small niches containing images of Buddha, though these cannot be seen from the courtyard. The sanctum wall has three more Buddha images on its outer side, and these can be seen from outside.Two staircases can be found on the northeastern and southeastern corners, both of which lead up to the first floor. The first floor has four turrets, one in each corner. The northeastern and southeastern turrets have openings that face one another, whilst the other two turrets have openings that face to the east. The first floor also contains an image of Akṣobhya Buddha at the center of its sanctum. Three other niches on the exterior wall of the sanctum house smaller images of Buddha facing in each of the four cardinal directions. Two staircases at the northeast and southeast corners of the sanctum lead up to the second floor, which is home to astūpa. Thestūpais roofed in brick corbel and supported by four stone pillars. There are four openings, one in each of the four cardinal directions. The third and fourth floors of the sanctum both containmaṇḍala,whilst the topmost sixth floor houses astūpawith achatra. The pinnacle of theśikharais astūpabased on theāmalaka.According toBhikṣu(1981, 24), a total of 3341 Buddha images are attached to the outer wall of the temple. These images vary widely in size.The main sanctum is on the ground floor of the temple and contains an east-facing terracotta image of Akṣobhya. The statue is enshrined behind a glass door. To the right of Akṣobhya, one can find statues of Ratnagarbha, Mahāmañjuśrī and Amoghapāśa Lokeśvara, while Prajñāpāramitā and Vajrāṅkuśa are to his left. Various other deities are placed outside of the glass door, such as a statue of Samantabhadra to the right and Vajrapāṇi to the left. An image of Dīpaṅkara is attached to the southern wall of the sanctum and an image of Maitreya can be found on the northern wall. Outside the sanctum, more small rooms house further images; the southern, western and northern rooms contain statues of Ratnapāṇi, Padmapāṇi and Viśvapāṇi respectively.Four turrets have been erected on the first floor of the temple. The sanctum on this floor contains images of Amitābha. A Svayambhūcaitya, Vāgīśvaradharmadhātumaṇḍala, Vajradhātumaṇḍala and Sarvabuddha Mahākūṭa Śūnyanirañjanacaitya(acaityaof absolute and pure emptiness) are located on the second, third, fourth and fifth floor respectively (seeŚākya1988, 10). The temple has acaityaas its finial.Aāgamahouse for the goddess Vidyādharī has been constructed to the east of the temple. Originally, this was the house of Abhayarāja, the man who built the Mahābuddha Temple. The goddess is theāgamadeity of this house. She appeared to Abhayarāja in a dream, ordering him to construct the Mahābuddha temple in the courtyard of his house. The ground floor of theāgamabuilding contains a place for chantingbhajana. According toŚākya(1988, 10) a secret image of Vidyādharīdevī is kept on the first floor. Apura(phucā) can be found on the top of the temple with five metal finials above it.Aśikhara-style temple of Māyādevī can be found in the southwestern corner of the courtyard. This corner also contains a platform (ḍabalī).The style of Mahābuddha Temple resembles the Mahābodhi Temple of Patan (Gutschow 1997, 308 andŚākya1988, 10). King Amara Malla appointed the man who constructed this temple, Abhayarāja, as the Head (nāikyā)Ḍiṭṭhāof manufacturing coins. As recorded in the chronicle (NBhV, 101), Abhayarāja was a lay Buddhistācāryaof Oṃkuli Vihāra and was a great devotee. He was also learned in various sciences. Estranged from his family due to a dispute, Abhayarāja began living in Bodh Gaya together with his younger wife. He returned to Kathmandu Valley in 1565 (NS 685) and started constructing this temple after hearing a voice in the sky: “O Abhayarāja, Mahābauddha is pleased with your devotion. Mahābauddha will come into your house. You do not need to stay here. Return to your house and build a temple. Mahābauddha will come to reside in the temple. You will also receive a royal honor. I am the goddess Vidyādharī, the servant of Mahābauddha” (NBhV, 101).Before its completion, however, he passed away. His youngest son, Buddhaju (Baudd haju) therefore took on the task. Buddhaju also passed away after completing the second floor, and his son Jīvarāja and grandson Jayamuni completed the construction in 1601 (NS 721).Śākya(1988, 10-11) writes that King Śivasiṃha Malla was invited to the opening ceremony of the temple in 1601. However,Gutschow(1997, 308 and 2011, 516) records two different dates: he argues that the temple was completed in 1602 and was consecrated in April 1610 on the auspicious day ofakṣaya tṛṭīyāby King Śivasiṃha. Gutschow also notes that the chronicles consistently replace the termbodhiwithbauddha;“the village is called not Bodh Gayā but Bauddha Gayā; the temple in Nepal is not the Bodhi temple but the Mahābauddha temple, which is consecrated to the Great Buddha” (Gutschow1997, 308). He further adds that the temple was partially renovated in 1776 (ibid. 308). The four upper storeys collapsed during the earthquake in January 1934.For a detailed archtiectural description seeGutschow1997 (308-312) andGutschow2011 (516-520).
description_ne: ललितपुर सुन्धाराबाट दक्षिणतर्फको बाटो भई ओकु बाहाल जाँदा बाटोको पश्चिमपट्टि महाबुद्ध मन्दिर पूर्वाभिमुख गरी अवस्थित छ । टेराकोटा इँटबाट निर्मित शिखरशैलीको यस मन्दिरको प्रत्येक इँटमा बुद्धमूर्ति देखिने हुनाले सामान्यत: यसलाई महाबुद्ध मन्दिर भनिए पनि वास्तवमा यो एउटा विहार हो । संस्कृतमा यसलाई बोधिमण्डप विहार भनिन्छ । यो विहार ओकु बाहा: (रुद्रवर्ण महाविहार) को शाखा हो । भिक्षु सुदर्शन (Bhikṣu Sudarśana 1981, 24) दिएको जानकारी अनुसार यस मन्दिरमा जम्मा ३३४१ बुद्धमूर्तिहरू राखिएका छन् । बाटो छेउमै विहारभित्र पस्ने मूल ढोका रहेको छ । नयाँ प्रविधि प्रयोग गरी सिमेन्ट प्लाष्टर गरी बनाइएको यस ढोकामा अष्टमङ्गल सहित विविध बुट्टाहरू राखी सजाइएको छ । मूल ढोकाबाट भित्र पसेपछि साँघुरो गल्ली हुँदै केही पर पुगेपछि अर्को ढोका राखिएको छ । उक्त ढोकाबाट भित्र छिरेर महाकाल, गणेश, हारतीको मूर्ति राखिएको बाटो पार गरेपछि विहारको चोकमा पुगिन्छ । विहार प्राङ्गणको बीचमा ६ तलाको मन्दिर उभिएको छ । भुइँतलामा मन्दिरको गर्भगृह रहेको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र शीशाको ढोकाभित्र पूर्वाभिमुख गरी टेराकोटाको अक्षोभ्य बुद्धको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । अक्षोभ्यको दक्षिणमा रत्नगर्भ, महामञ्जुश्री र अमोघपाश लोकेश्वर राखिएका छन् भने उत्तरमा प्रज्ञापारमिता र वज्राङ्कुश छन् । गर्भगृहभित्रै शीशाबाहिर पनि विविध मूर्ति राखिएका छन् । अक्षोभ्यको दक्षिणमा समन्तभद्र र उत्तरमा वज्रपाणि राखिएका छन् । त्यस्तै गर्भगृहको दक्षिणी भित्तामा दीपङ्कर र उत्तरी भित्तामा मैत्रेय राखिएका छन् । मन्दिरको बाहिरी भागमा पनि कोठा बनाएर देवताहरू स्थापना गरिएका छन् । दक्षिणतिर रहेको कोठामा रत्नपाणि, पश्चिमतिर रहेको कोठामा पद्मपाणि र उत्तरतिर रहेको कोठामा विश्वपाणि रहेका छन् । मन्दिरको पहिलो तलामा कौसी जस्तो निकालेर चार कुनामा चारवटा शिखरशैलीकोकचादेग:(turret) बनाइएको छ । यस तलामा अमिताभ बुद्ध राखिएको छ । दोस्रो तलामा स्वयम्भू चैत्य, तेस्रो तलामा वागीश्वर धर्मधातु मण्डल, चौथो तलामा वज्रधातु मण्डल र पाँचौँ तलामा सर्वबुद्ध महाकूट शून्यनिरञ्जन चैत्य (Stupa of absolutely pure emptiness) स्थापना गरिएको छ (Śākya 1988, 10) । मन्दिरको सबभन्दा माथि गजूरको रूपमा चैत्य राखिएको छ ।मन्दिरको अगाडि पूर्वमा विद्याधरीदेवीको आगमघर रहेको छ । यो घर महाबुद्ध मन्दिर बनाउने अभयराजको हो र विद्याधरीदेवी त्यस घरको आगम-देवता थिइन् । विद्याधरीदेवीबाट सपनामा आज्ञा भएबमोजिम अभयराजले आफ्नो घरको आँगनमा मन्दिर बनाएका थिए । त्यसैले महाबुद्ध मन्दिरभन्दा विद्याधरीदेवीको मन्दिर पुरानो हो । आगमघरको भुइँतलामा नामसंगीति भजन गाउने व्यवस्था गरिएको छ । आगमघरको पहिलो तलामा आगमघरको विद्याधरीदेवी गुह्य मूर्ति राखिएको छ । आगमघरको माथि छानामा अन्य विहारमा जस्तै पुर (फुचा) बनाएर पाँचवटा धातुको गजूर चढाइएको छ । मन्दिर परिसरको दक्षिण-पश्चिम कुनामा मायादेवीको शिखरशैलीको अर्को एउटा सानो मन्दिर बनाइएको छ । मन्दिरको पूर्वतिर डबली पनि बनाइएको छ ।यो मन्दिर भारतको महाबोधि मन्दिरवाट प्रभावित भई बनाइएको हो । यो मन्दिर निर्माणको श्रेय अभयराज शाक्यलाई जान्छ । उनी राजा अमर मल्लका पालामा मुद्रा विभागका प्रमुख भई काम गर्थे । उनी पारिवारिक कलहले गर्दा विरक्तिएर कान्छी श्रीमतीसहित भारतको बुद्धगया गएर बसे । त्यहाँ सपनामा विद्याधरीदेवीबाट आदेश भएबमोजिम नेपाल फर्केर नेसं ६८५ देखि यो मन्दिर बनाउन शुरु गरे । तर उक्त कार्य पूरा हुन नपाउँदै उनको मृत्यु भयो । त्यसपछि अभयराजका कान्छा छोरा बुद्धजुले मन्दिर निर्माणको कार्य अगाडि बढाए । तर दुई तला पूरा भएपछि उनको पनि मृत्यु भयो । बुद्धजुको छोरा जीवराजले आफ्नो छोरा जयमुनिको सहयोग लिएर नेसं ७२१ मा मन्दिर निर्माणको काम पूरा गरे । मन्दिर उद्घाटन समारोहमा राजा शिवसिंह मल्ललाई निमन्त्रणा गरिएको थियो । यसप्रकार चार पुस्ताको परिश्रमबाट ३६ वर्ष लगाएर यो मन्दिर बनेको देखिन्छ ।विसं १९९० को भूकम्पले मन्दिरको भुइँतलाभन्दा माथिको सम्पूर्ण भाग भत्केको थियो । विसं २०७२ को भूकम्पले चर्केको मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार कार्य अहिले अन्तिम चरणमा पुगेको छ ।तिब्बतीहरू यस मन्दिरलाईYe-rang sangs-rgyas stong sku(The Thousand Buddhas of Patan) भन्ने गर्छन् (Dowman 1981, 246) । महाबुद्ध मन्दिरको सम्मान स्वरूप सन् १९४९ मा ८ पैसाको हुलाक टिकट निकालिएको थियो भने सन् १९७१ मा निकालिएको रू. १ को नोटमा महाबुद्धको चित्र अंकित गरिएको थियो ।
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages)

historical_events.event_description: The earthquake of 1934 severely damaged the temple. Aside from the ground floor, all of the floors collapsed.

A ceremony was held to celebrate the completion of the reconstruction work. Juddha Śamaśera, the Prime Minister of Nepal, was invited to participate in theMahā Ahorātra Yajña.The Prime Minister rebated the loan instantly and distributed cash prizes to the tutors, priests, and artisans. The temple was rebuilt on a slightly smaller scale after it was destroyed in the 1934 earthquake (Bernier1978, 75).
Indrānanda constructed the Dharmahātu Maṇḍala on the death anniversary of his deceased father Ghanānanda
Abhayarāja Śākya started to construct the temple.
To protect the temple from damage caused by heat and rain, local people and artisans working under the Mahābuddha Mandir Saṃrakṣaṇa Samiti repaired some of the images.

The earthquake of 2015 severely affected the temple. The temple was badly damaged and was about to collapse. Local people immediately launched a restoration project without any government support. The restoration work is now finished and preparations for a ceremony to celebrate its completion are underway.

Construction of Mahabuddha Temple was completed by Abhayarāja Śākya's grandson Jīvarāja and great grandson Jayamuni, following a model that Abhayarāja allegedly brought with him from Bodh Gaya (Gutschow2011, 516). King Shivasiṃha Malla was invited to participate in the worship ritual that was organised upon completion of the work. Siddhidevaju was the chiefācāryaon this occasion.

Paṇḍita Jīvarāja and Jayamuni went to Sikkim and offered a plate ofprasādafrom the Mahabuddha enshrined in thisvihārato the King of Sikkim. Grateful for this offering, the king filled the plate with gold. When Jayamuni returned with the gold, he called a meeting of the members of thesaṅghato determine what to do with it. They decided to make fixtures (side panels for the four sides, thetoraṇas, and the decorations above thetoraṇasfor the chariot) of the Red Matsyendranātha. These fixtures were placed upon the chariot for the first time in NS 774 upon its arrival to Gāḥ Bāhāḥ. Aguṭhīwas then set up to ensure the safekeeping and maintenance of the fixtures. Thisguṭhīwas known as theLusa Guṭhī,
